question: Should the shared `userInitiated` provider-interaction context be an approved capability for CLI browser-cookie import, or should Grok restrict this permission to the cookie-refresh command specifically?
rationale: Both choices can satisfy the reported refresh failure, but they establish different long-term Keychain and browser-cookie access boundaries that source inspection alone cannot safely choose.

options.title: Approve the shared context contract
options.body: Keep the implementation and require focused coverage or documentation that ordinary and scheduled CLI fetches never receive the user-initiated context.

options.title: Narrow the permission to refresh
options.body: Pass an explicit refresh-only capability into the Grok strategy so future user-triggered CLI actions cannot inherit browser-cookie import authority unintentionally.

recommendation.title: Approve the shared context contract
recommendation.body: Keep the implementation and require focused coverage or documentation that ordinary and scheduled CLI fetches never receive the user-initiated context.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main provider descriptor and fetch-plan refactor places this trust-boundary decision in the provider architecture they most recently changed.
